Normalise raw 'Scopus' entries to a stable tidy schema

Source: R/combine.R, R/plot-analyse.R, R/records.R
scopus_records.Rd

Converts the nested list returned by the 'Scopus' Search API into a flat, predictable tibble with one row per record. This shape is the common currency of the package. Both scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() return it, and the DOI, comparison and export helpers all consume it.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'scopus_records'
as_tibble(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'scopus_records'
as.data.frame(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'scopus_records'
autoplot(object, ...)

scopus_records(
  x,
  query = NA_character_,
  view = NULL,
  fields = c("core", "extended")
)

is_scopus_records(x)

Arguments

x

An object to test.

...

Ignored, for S3 compatibility.

object

A scopus_records object (for the autoplot() method).

query

Optional character scalar recording the query that produced the entries, kept in the query column for provenance.

view

Optional character scalar naming the Search API view the entries came from. Pass "COMPLETE" to read authors from the author list that view carries and to add an authkeywords column (see below). Any other value, including the default NULL, reads the first author and reproduces the original columns exactly, so existing callers that never mention view see no change at all. scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() pass this through automatically.

fields

"core" (the default) builds the columns listed under Value, exactly as before. "extended" also keeps the document type, source type, volume, issue, pages, ISSN, PubMed identifier and open-access status the Search API sends with every record, and under view = "COMPLETE" the abstract, at no extra quota (see Extended fields). scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() pass this through.

Value

The coercion methods return a plain tibble or data frame with the same columns and the scopus_records class removed.

The autoplot() method returns a ggplot2::ggplot of the records per year. The bars cover every year the set's plan searched, a year without records drawn as a zero bar, and no year the plan did not search. A plan over 2015, 2016, 2019 and 2020 therefore draws no bar for 2017 or 2018. A harvest stopped before its last cell covers only the cells it ran. Without a plan, or with one that sent no year limit, the bars run from the first year in the records to the last. When a max_results cap stopped any cell of the retrieval, a caption says that the bars count records retrieved, not publications per year. When the years plotted reach the year of the recorded retrieved_at, the caption also says that year was incomplete when the records were retrieved, as plot_scopus_trend() does.

A tibble of class scopus_records with the columns entry_number (integer), scopus_id (character), doi (character), title (character), authors (character, the author list under view = "COMPLETE" and the first author otherwise, as Details explains), year (integer, the leading four digits of the cover date), date (character, the ISO cover date), publication (character, the source title), citations (integer) and query (character). A missing field becomes NA, and an empty result set yields a zero-row tibble with the same columns. When view = "COMPLETE", an authkeywords column is added: the author-supplied keywords the 'Scopus' Search API returns under that view, as a single string in 'Scopus' own " | "-delimited form (NA when the document has none, or when the API omits the field for a given key's entitlement; see Details). With fields = "extended", the character columns doc_type, doc_type_description, source_type, volume, issue, pages, issn and pubmed_id follow, then the integer open_access and, under view = "COMPLETE", the character abstract. doc_type and doc_type_description hold the document-type code and name 'Scopus' gives the record, such as "ar" and "Article", and source_type holds the source type, such as "Journal". issn is the print ISSN as 'Scopus' writes it, without the hyphen, kept as text so its leading zeros survive. open_access is the open-access status code (see Extended fields).

is_scopus_records() returns a length-one logical.

Details

The 'Scopus' API signals an empty result set with a single sentinel entry that carries an error field and no identifier. This is detected and turned into a zero-row result, with no spurious record in it, while a genuine record that also carries a per-entry error annotation is kept.

What authors holds depends on the view. The Search API's dc:creator field is the first author alone under either view, in the indexed form 'Scopus' uses ("Zhang F."). The author list arrives only under view = "COMPLETE", as the author objects Elsevier's views table lists for that view alone. A STANDARD record therefore names its first author, and a tally of STANDARD authors counts first authorships. A harvest records its view in the view attribute (see scopus_fetch()), and scopus_top() and as_bibliometrix() say once per session that a set retrieved under STANDARD names first authors only. Under COMPLETE, each author is written as "Surname, Given", as the surname alone when the given name is missing or empty, or as the indexed name when the surname is missing. Exact duplicates are dropped. The API lists at most 100 authors per record, and its author-count field gives the total. A record whose list names nobody falls back to dc:creator. The Python twin builds the same string from pybliometrics' author_names in the common case, and parts company at two edges. Where an author object lacks a surname or given-name key, pybliometrics builds no list, so that twin keeps the first author while this one lists every author. Where a surname is null or empty, pybliometrics writes the given name after a bare comma, and this package uses the indexed name.

Author keywords are only ever present under view = "COMPLETE"; the STANDARD view (the default throughout the package) never includes them, and authkeywords is not added to the output at all in that case, so existing code that inspects the column names of a STANDARD-view result is unaffected. Even under COMPLETE view, some 'Scopus' API keys do not return populated author keywords (this was observed directly against a live, otherwise fully-entitled key during development, on documents that do carry author keywords in 'Scopus' itself); if your own keywords come back all NA, the field is most likely gated by your account's entitlement rather than genuinely absent, and is worth raising with your 'Scopus'/Elsevier account contact.

Extended fields

Elsevier's Search views table lists every field fields = "extended" reads under both views, except the abstract (dc:description), which only the COMPLETE view carries. They arrive in the responses a retrieval already pays for, so they cost no extra quota. A COMPLETE harvest returns up to 25 abstracts with each request, while scopus_abstract() spends one request per record from the separate Abstract Retrieval quota.

doc_type holds the code the DOCTYPE() search field takes. Elsevier's search tips list the codes with their names: ar for an article, re a review, cp a conference paper, er an erratum and others. A retracted item carries tb, which that list leaves out. The 'Scopus' Content Coverage Guide (section 3.1) defines an erratum as a report of an error, correction or retraction of a previously published paper, so er covers retraction notices as well as corrections. The guide gives an article the type Retracted once a retraction notice for it is published. These codes are the labels 'Scopus' assigns, and they do not screen a set for retractions, since 'Scopus' does not label every retracted item (Ortega and Delgado-Quirós, 2024). Check a set against the Retraction Watch database, which Crossref makes openly available, before relying on it. summary() reports how many records 'Scopus' labels er and tb. Errata can also be left out of the search itself with AND NOT DOCTYPE(er), joined by scopus_query(), which brackets the rest of the query first, since 'Scopus' applies AND NOT last (see Examples).

open_access holds the code 'Scopus' sends in its openaccess field. Elsevier's Scopus APIs Getting Started Guide (section 17) illustrates its values with 0 for a record that is not open access, 1 for gold and 2 for green. The column therefore holds a status code, which can take values other than 0 and 1.

References

Elsevier. (2023). Scopus APIs getting started guide (Version 1). https://dev.elsevier.com/guides/Scopus%20API%20Guide_V1_20230907.pdf

Elsevier. (2023). Scopus content coverage guide. https://supportcontent.elsevier.com/Support%20Hub/Scopus/Scopus_ContentCoverage_Guide_WEB.pdf

Ortega, J. L., & Delgado-Quirós, L. (2024). The indexation of retracted literature in seven principal scholarly databases: A coverage comparison of Dimensions, OpenAlex, PubMed, Scilit, Scopus, The Lens and Web of Science. Scientometrics, 129(7), 3769–3785. doi:10.1007/s11192-024-05034-y

Examples

# An entry in the shape the Search API returns it. The fields are those of
# a real article, taken from the bundled `example_records`, which stands in
# for a harvest because 'Scopus' records may not be redistributed. It
# carries no 'Scopus' identifier, so `dc:identifier` is absent and
# `scopus_id` comes back NA, as it does for any unidentified record.
raw <- list(entry = list(
  list(
    `prism:doi` = "10.1021/am509065d",
    `dc:title` = "Flexible and Stackable Laser-Induced Graphene Supercapacitors",
    `dc:creator` = "Zhiwei Peng",
    `prism:publicationName` = "ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces",
    `prism:coverDate` = "2015-01-13",
    `citedby-count` = "469"
  )
))
scopus_records(raw, query = 'TITLE-ABS-KEY("graphene supercapacitor")')
#> <scopus_records> 1 record
#> query: "TITLE-ABS-KEY(\"graphene supercapacitor\")"
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   entry_number scopus_id doi     title authors  year date  publication citations
#>          <int> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr>   <int> <chr> <chr>           <int>
#> 1            1 NA        10.102… Flex… Zhiwei…  2015 2015… ACS Applie…       469

# Under COMPLETE view an entry may also carry author keywords, which the
# Search API returns in its own " | "-delimited form. The bundled corpus
# holds no keywords, so the ones below are illustrative.
raw_complete <- list(entry = list(
  list(
    `prism:doi` = "10.1021/am509065d",
    `dc:title` = "Flexible and Stackable Laser-Induced Graphene Supercapacitors",
    authkeywords = "graphene | supercapacitor | energy storage"
  )
))
scopus_records(raw_complete, view = "COMPLETE")
#> <scopus_records> 1 record
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   entry_number scopus_id doi     title authors  year date  publication citations
#>          <int> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr>   <int> <chr> <chr>           <int>
#> 1            1 NA        10.102… Flex… NA         NA NA    NA                 NA
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: query <chr>, authkeywords <chr>

# fields = "extended" keeps the fields both views send beyond the core ones.
# The volume, issue, pages and print ISSN below are the article's own. The
# document type and source type are illustrative, since the bundled corpus
# came from OpenAlex and records no 'Scopus' labels.
raw_extended <- list(entry = list(
  list(
    `prism:doi` = "10.1021/am509065d",
    `dc:title` = "Flexible and Stackable Laser-Induced Graphene Supercapacitors",
    subtype = "ar",
    subtypeDescription = "Article",
    `prism:aggregationType` = "Journal",
    `prism:volume` = "7",
    `prism:issueIdentifier` = "5",
    `prism:pageRange` = "3414-3419",
    `prism:issn` = "19448244"
  )
))
extended <- scopus_records(raw_extended, fields = "extended")
as.data.frame(extended)[, c("doc_type", "volume", "issue", "pages", "issn")]
#>   doc_type volume issue     pages     issn
#> 1       ar      7     5 3414-3419 19448244

# Errata can be left out of the search itself. scopus_query() brackets the
# rest of the query, since 'Scopus' applies AND NOT last.
scopus_query(
  scopus_query("graphene", "graphite", .op = "OR", .field = "TITLE-ABS-KEY"),
  "DOCTYPE(er)", .op = "AND NOT"
)
#> [1] "(TITLE-ABS-KEY(graphene) OR TITLE-ABS-KEY(graphite)) AND NOT DOCTYPE(er)"

# An object already in this schema is returned unchanged.
identical(scopus_records(example_records), example_records)
#> [1] TRUE
